# SGP4 reference fixture provenance

`vallado.json` contains **verification fixtures, not live observations**.

Source: Vallado, Crawford, Hujsak & Kelso, *Revisiting Spacetrack Report #3*,
AIAA 2006-6753, https://celestrak.org/publications/AIAA/2006-6753/.
The inputs and expected vectors were extracted from `SGP4-VER.TLE` and
`tcppver.out`, distributed with the locked python-sgp4 2.27 package:
https://github.com/brandon-rhodes/python-sgp4.

Source file SHA-256 digests (full packaged files):

- SGP4-VER.TLE: `d246d1d9d768ace445a38a965713fa9ba52d80fd8a41a0502ff83d7acffe2881`
- tcppver.out: `687bf28dbe52df86e8e60ab5cb4a08d1aa3dbcaf4e63b1f7ab95f044fbe3833b`

For each catalog number 5, 4632, 8195 and 14128, the fixture includes the two
69-character TLE lines and the first three published time-offset vectors. These
cover near-Earth, deep-space and resonant orbits, including negative propagation
time. Expected position/velocity numbers were copied from `tcppver.out`, not
calculated using OrbitIQ or Python SGP4. OMM-format inputs were converted from
the reference TLE using python-sgp4's `export_omm` once when creating this fixture;
conversion does not generate the expected output vectors.

Vectors are Earth-centered TEME, position in km, velocity in km/s. Time offsets
are minutes from each input epoch. Tests run both the TLE engine path and the
OMM engine path against these fixed published numbers. Absolute tolerances are
`1e-5 km` for position and `1e-8 km/s` for velocity, with relative tolerance zero.
These allow printed output precision and sub-microsecond epoch rounding through
Python datetime. They measure numerical implementation agreement, not the
accuracy of a real satellite's predicted location or uncertainty.

Phase 2 adds `vallado-leo.json` without modifying `vallado.json` or any original
reference assertion. It copies catalog cases 6251 (low-perigee normal-drag LEO)
and 28057 (CBERS 2, nearly circular LEO) at 0, 120, 1440 and 2880 minutes from the
same two published source files and source hashes above. Both TLE and OMM paths
are compared, adding 16 comparisons at the unchanged tolerances. Original
negative-time deep-space cases remain part of the 24 baseline comparisons.

Run the full audit with:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=backend uv run --locked python scripts/verify_scientific_references.py --output docs/phase-2-reference-results.json
```

The output records every fixture identity/hash, source epoch, input element set,
requested propagation time, expected and actual vectors, per-component error,
frame, units, tolerances and pass/fail. It exits nonzero on any failed comparison.
Timezone equivalence, fractional-offset and boundary tests are separate
self-consistency tests. The Astropy UTC Julian-day check validates the time input
independently, not the orbital vectors or a coordinate transformation.

## Phase 3 terrestrial references

`earth-fixed.json` is a separate reference fixture. Existing SGP4 fixtures and
assertions are unchanged. Expected outputs are transcribed from the sources
below, never generated by OrbitIQ. Runtime does not read this test fixture.

- Vallado, Crawford, Hujsak & Kelso, **AIAA-2006-6753-Rev2**, Appendix C, printed
  page 32, TEME -> ITRF example at 2004-04-06 07:51:28.386 UTC.
  https://celestrak.org/publications/AIAA/2006-6753/AIAA-2006-6753-Rev2.pdf
  Retrieved in this phase; PDF SHA-256:
  `538a5c0ea174eb569bbc258011717142a26d72871ab07cc64ee5fa3773164b16`.
  Position/velocity, DUT1, TAI-UTC and polar motion are literal paper values.
  The paper's input y is **6127.64465950 km** and output y **7901.29527540 km**;
  the upstream Astropy test has slightly different transcription digits. We
  retain the original paper values here. Test both published fixed EOP and the
  actual local IERS final values. Fixed EOP are a **reference-only table**, never
  a configured application fallback or invented satellite observation.
- Astropy **7.2.3**, official `docs/coordinates/satellites.rst`:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astropy/astropy/v7.2.3/docs/coordinates/satellites.rst
  SHA-256 `493bf8bbf7a566de2d140765810e9f4d46f41e1c3b57c557549fa0debe1cf0cd`.
  The example's TLE, UTC Julian date and printed WGS84 geodetic result are copied.
  Microsecond datetime representation differs from the printed JD by less than
  one microsecond. This independently specified example tests the wrapper's full
  SGP4/TEME/ITRS/geodetic path at a second epoch. It uses the same established
  library stack, not an independent observation or alternate dynamical model.
- Official SOFA/ERFA `t_gc2gd`, `t_utctai`, `t_utcut1` reference constants, also
  in locked pyerfa **2.0.1.5** `erfa/tests/test_ufunc.py`:
  https://github.com/liberfa/erfa/blob/v2.0.1/src/t_erfa_c.c
  WGS84 geocentric input is [2000000,3000000,5244000] metres. Longitude and
  latitude reference radians, height, two-part UTC/TAI/UT1 dates and controlled
  DUT1 are transcribed. Expected outputs do not call OrbitIQ or Astropy.

Tolerances, relative tolerance always zero:

| Reference | Position / height | Velocity / angles / time | Reason and scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vallado fixed published EOP | 2e-5 km (2 cm), Cartesian components | 1e-6 km/s (1 mm/s) | Deliberate centimetre-level numerical check, stricter than Astropy's official 30-cm / 1-cm/s reference check; accommodates convention/reference finite precision and finite-difference velocity; does not claim printed-digit agreement |
| Vallado bundled final EOP | 3e-4 km (30 cm) | 1e-5 km/s (1 cm/s) | Upstream Astropy reference tolerance with updated IERS values; published and modern final EOP differ |
| Astropy official satellite example | 1e-4 km (10 cm) height | 1e-5 deg angles (about 1.1 m of surface arc at equator) | Full-chain check with updated final EOP and rounded JD/example output; not positional uncertainty |
| SOFA WGS84 geodesy | 1e-10 km height (1e-7 m) | 1e-10 deg | Double precision comparison of a mathematical ellipsoid; not geophysical accuracy |
| SOFA UTC->TAI/UT1 | Not spatial | 1e-6 s | Two-part dates avoid single-JD cancellation; numerical time conversion only |

Actual fixed-EOP Vallado residual is about **1.32 cm**, not zero; its exact source
has not been isolated to one rounding/convention term. No sub-centimetre claim is
made. The 2-cm criterion was not relaxed. Full actual vectors, EOP, errors and
limits are recorded by `scripts/verify_earth_fixed_references.py` in
`docs/phase-3-reference-results.json`. The bundled-EOP maximum position residual
is about 28.36 cm. These limited examples do not establish universal ITRS,
velocity, polar-region or orbit prediction accuracy.

Analytic WGS84 axes/poles use independently specified semi-major radius,
flattening and a 400-km ellipsoidal height. Wrapping/antimeridian, failures,
configuration, sampling and concurrency tests are boundary/contract checks,
not additional published orbit references. No test downloads external resources.
